_about: C-129: CALLOW SCHOOL. floors: 1F-7F, each a TEXTBOOK chapter (subject) whose five topics are the floor's board, word for word; a chapter is greyed until its visited_flag is set. paper: the exam's seven sections in order; answer is an index into choices (the save stores 1-4 for A-D, 0 unanswered). The mark is round(correct * 100 / total); pass_mark or better passes, and passing gives the DIPLOMA (flags.diploma). The save keeps no letter: grades turns a mark into it (GradeLetter). vars: u16s at sb1_vars + 2 * (number - vars_start); answers is the first of the vars holding each question's answer, per_var to a var, three bits each, question q in var answers + q // per_var at bit 3 * (q % per_var).

floors.subject: LANGUAGE
floors.placard:
1F  LANGUAGE

What a word points at, how words
come apart, and why their order
matters.

Everything else here is taught
in words, so words come first.

The syllabus is on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
1F  LANGUAGE

TOPICS: NAMES, PIECES, ORDER,
AMBIGUITY, SPELLING.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.
floors.board_intro:
The board is written up neatly,
in five parts.

board.text:
A name is a handle.

It lets you point at a thing
without having to carry it.

Rename a thing and it stays
exactly what it was.

Only the handle moved.

Words come apart.

UN-READ-ABLE is three pieces.
Each one means something alone.

Learn the pieces, and you can read
words nobody taught you.

Same words, different order.

USER READS DAEMON.
DAEMON READS USER.

Nothing was added. Nothing was
taken away.

Everything changed.

One word can carry several
meanings.

A BOX holds a daemon.
A BOX is where you tick a YES.

The words around it decide
which one you meant.

Spelling is a rule for turning
a sound into marks.

The rule is old, and full of
exceptions.

Nobody is under a spell.

In the corner, in smaller chalk,
someone has added: UNDER A SPELL.

It is underlined twice.

floors.subject: ATTENTION
floors.placard:
2F  ATTENTION

What gets looked at, and what that
costs everything else.

You cannot keep what you never
noticed, so this comes before
MEMORY.

The syllabus is on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
2F  ATTENTION

TOPICS: LIMITS, CUES, SEARCH,
SWITCHING, MISSED.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.
floors.board_intro:
The board is written up neatly,
in five parts.

board.text:
There is only so much of it.

More on one thing is less on
everything else.

It is never added. Only moved.

A cue says where to look before
the thing arrives.

A good cue makes you faster.

A wrong one makes you slower than
no cue at all.

The more things there are, the
longer the one you want takes...

...unless it is the only thing that
is different.

The odd one out finds you.

Changing what you attend to costs
time, every time.

Two things at once is nearly always
one thing, then the other, fast.

Watch one thing closely enough and
something unmissable walks past.

Nobody who missed it believes
they did.

floors.subject: MEMORY
floors.placard:
3F  MEMORY

What is kept, what fades, and what
changes each time you take it out.

The syllabus is on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
3F  MEMORY

TOPICS: STORING, FADING,
CROWDING, RECALL, SPACING.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.
floors.board_intro:
The board is written up neatly,
in five parts.

board.text:
Nothing is kept whole.

What is kept is enough to build
it again.

Left alone, it fades.

Fastest at first. Then slower.
Never quite to nothing.

New things push on old ones, and
old on new.

The most alike are the most
easily confused.

Remembering is not reading a copy.

It is building one, and the build
is saved over the old.

Remember it often enough, and
you remember the remembering.

Once a day for seven days beats
seven times in one day.

Nobody believes this until they
try it.

floors.subject: CATEGORIES
floors.placard:
4F  CATEGORIES

How things are sorted, and why the
edges will not hold still.

The syllabus is on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
4F  CATEGORIES

TOPICS: MIDDLES, EDGES, FEATURES,
LEVELS, OTHER.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.
floors.board_intro:
The board is written up neatly,
in five parts.

board.text:
Most kinds have a middle: the best
example, the one that comes first.

Everything else is more or less
like it.

No kind has a clean edge.

Somewhere there is always a thing
that is half in.

Sorting looks at a handful of
features.

Pick the wrong ones, and two very
different things share a drawer.

The same thing sits in several
kinds at once, at different heights.

A thing. A kind of thing.
A kind of kind.

Every way of sorting ends up with a
drawer called OTHER.

Watch how fast it fills.

floors.subject: LEARNING
floors.placard:
5F  LEARNING

How a mind changes itself, one
small join at a time.

The syllabus is on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
5F  LEARNING

TOPICS: CONNECTIONS, PRACTICE,
THRESHOLD, FEEDBACK, PRUNING.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.

board.text:
A mind is cells joined to cells.

Each join has a strength: how hard
one cell pushes the next when it
fires.

Use a join and it grows stronger.

Cells that fire together wire
together, as the saying goes.

A cell fires only when the pushes
on it add up past a line.

Some cells sit close to that line.
They fire at almost nothing.

Learning needs to find out how it
went.

Without that, practice only makes
a habit, not a skill.

Joins that are never used are
taken away.

Growing up is losing most of them,
on purpose.

floors.subject: BIAS
floors.placard:
6F  BIAS

The ways a mind leans, and the
arguments that only look sound.

The syllabus is on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
6F  BIAS

TOPICS: FRAMING, ANCHORS,
CONFIRMING, HINDSIGHT, FALLACIES.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.

board.text:
Ninety in a hundred survive.
Ten in a hundred die.

It is the same number. People
choose differently between them.

The way a thing is put is doing
the choosing.

The first number heard pulls every
guess after it toward itself.

Even when everyone knows it was
picked at random.

People look for what agrees with
them, and find it.

What disagrees gets checked twice
as hard.

Once you know how it ended, it
looks as if it had to end that way.

It did not.

A fallacy is an argument that
looks as if it works.

Attacking the speaker. Two choices
where there are more.

Everybody does it, so it is fine.

floors.subject: ERROR
floors.placard:
7F  ERROR

Being wrong, and why that is where
the change happens.

The last floor. The syllabus is
on the desk.
floors.syllabus:
COURSE SYLLABUS
7F  ERROR

TOPICS: SURPRISE, CORRECTION,
STEPS, MISTAKES, CERTAINTY.

All of it is on the board.
The exam covers the board.

PASS MARK: 80 out of 100.

board.text:
A mind is always guessing what
comes next.

Surprise is the size of the miss.

Learning is mostly correcting.

The bigger the miss, the bigger
the correction.

Correct too much at once and you
overshoot.

Small corrections, many times,
get closer.

A mistake you notice teaches more
than an answer you were given.

Being sure is not evidence.

Nothing surprises the surest, so
they learn the least.
